summary: New box Imperativ: example for sense 1 in Imperativ (MAC NE Old lady and a bird/37)

data.turoyo: ‘Hak̇a mazruqe mazráq, hak̇a əḥre ḥray, Ăḷo, lə+g̊fotaḥno qumax’.
data.translation: ‘If you pee, if you poop, by God, I shall not open it up for you (lit. ‘in front of you’)’.

summary: New idiom: ḥrele/ḥore ʕal daqno 'jemanden mit einer Bartbeschimpfung verächtlich machen'

data.headword: ḥrele/ḥore ʕal daqno 'jemanden mit einer Bartbeschimpfung verächtlich machen'
data.turoyo: ‘Hay ḥreli ʕal daqnux, ono uxlówayno aḥ+ḥalye, obówaynanne aḥ+ḥamuṣe’.
data.translation: ‘Screw you and your beard, I was the one eating the sweet ones, I gave them the sour ones’.
data.ref: MAC NE Old woman and a fox/37

rationale: A performative first-person insult rather than literal defecation. Lookup searches for daqn and ḥrela b found no existing version of the collocation; conventional status remains a question.

evidence.cite: MAC NE Old woman and a fox/37

summary: Bodily defecation is commonly objectless, but material/product NPs occur with the fox's eaten hens and the donkey's coins. Locations include qm u tarʕaṯxu, b dukṯe, bu ǧeməʕ and the affected b ruḥe.
koḥrele at 115/170 presents soiling discovered on hauling the man up. Its Preterit suffix supports ko-Preterit, rather than classification from German tense alone.

MAC NE Old woman and a fox/37 is a performative insult. JTM 5.2/32 is figurative destruction of a letter. The inherited mother/child crowding image at 65/267 is already glossed in its note and is left intact.

ḥroyo ḥrele is a cognate Infinitiv and Preterit pair; 6/93 already occurs in Infinitiv and is added only to the thin Preterit cell. The embedded 6/95 note counts as existing text and is not duplicated.
Is ḥreli ʕal daqnux a conventional beard insult, and is Hay part of the formula? The one attestation clearly expresses contempt.
Confirm ḥrəlli at PrS 74/119 and whether it indexes excreted material; no suffix decomposition is silently imposed.
Collate the inherited prs 236/11 and supplied PrS 81/28 numbering for the donkey clause before altering references.
Gold coins appear as a fantastic excreted product; a grain container is denied the ability to defecate in a riddle. Neither participant change establishes a new meaning.
